messages:
jane_support: hitting 401 invalid_api_key from our service after a recent key rotation. repro steps below, this started after we rolled some tenant changes earlier today. curl + response attached.

samir_eng: can you paste the exact curl you used (with redacted key)? also which org/account id are you calling against?

jane_support: here's the curl (redacted):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-*-redwood","input":"test"}'
```
Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or invalid"}
Org we're calling: org_87654. Key id shows as prefixed: ri-org1234-abcdef (we use multi-org keys in our infra).

eli_infra: quick thought: we recently added org-bound keys so the API will reject keys that have a different org prefix than the X-Org-ID or bound account. Do you set any org headers or override the org in your SDK?

jane_support: we don't set X-Org-ID currently. Our infra used to rely on the key implying the org. after the rotation we got a new key that has a different org prefix (ri-org1234 vs ri-org87654). could that be the issue?

samir_eng: yes likely. we shipped a guard: if a key is prefixed for a different org than the requested org (or the account associated with the request), we return 401. Two ways to reproduce quickly: 1) include X-Org-ID header matching the key prefix org; or 2) use a key that matches your tenant. can you try adding header: `X-Org-ID: org1234` and retry?

jane_support: trying now...

jane_support: still 401. here's the full request/response from our server (redacted):
```
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Api-Key REDACTED, Host: api.redwood.ai, User-Agent: our-service/1.2
Body: {"model":"gpt-*-redwood","input":"test"}
Response: 401 Unauthorized
Body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","code":"401","detail":"key org mismatch"}
```

eli_infra: that `detail` is helpful — backend is explicitly rejecting for org mismatch. are you proxying requests through another service (auth proxy) that might be stripping or rewriting headers? some proxies drop custom headers unless explicitly whitelisted.

ops_anna: also check that any service worker or edge cache isn't swapping the Authorization header. we saw cases where an edge rewrites host or adds its own org header for traffic shaping.

jane_support: ah — we do have an auth proxy in the path that inserts X-Org-ID based on session. turns out it was still configured for the old tenant id (org_87654) and not the new org_1234 in the rotated key. updating the proxy to set X-Org-ID: org1234 and retrying.

support-bot: note created ticket #SUP-2026 for root cause: proxy header mismatch on key rotation. assigned to samir_eng and eli_infra.

jane_support: after updating proxy header to org1234 the call now returns 200, tokens returned. thanks! :tada:

samir_eng: great. follow-up items: 1) we can add a clearer error message for org-bound key mismatch (include expected org) without leaking secrets; 2) add a diagnostic header in debug mode that echoes key prefix (redacted) to help repro; 3) doc note about proxies dropping custom headers.

eli_infra: i'll file a follow-up PR for the error text and a flag for `X-Debug-Org` that only appears when debug=true.

ops_anna: added action: check our onboarding doc to call out multi-org key rotations and proxy config.

jane_support: thank you team — closing this thread from my side.

support-bot: ticket #SUP-2026 marked resolved by jane_support.
